item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-22: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “I didn't go having us talk about Yalta, and if you look, Winston Churchill, Stalin, FDR - which was a big one - I didn't think about it.” Unsettled. An Anadolu Agency explainer dated Nov. 18, the day before the meeting, attributes the Yalta comparisons to news outlets, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Kremlin spokesman Peskov, not to Trump or the White House. Newsweek reports that Trump called the meeting "bigger than Yalta" and posted a Yalta image only after the meeting. No White House record of the trip could be read directly, and no record shows what Trump thought before the trip.

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-21: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Josh Shapiro)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “The problem is, the president didn't address it, didn't address AI, didn't push back on the Russians and their aggressions toward Ukraine, didn't do anything to push back on the work that China is doing to undermine our economy.” Unsettled. The joint U.S.-Russia-China declaration from the Nov. 19 Shenzhen summit says nothing on AI, Ukraine or Chinese economic practices. A White House release quotes Trump saying in a Fox News interview that he and Xi 'talked about' super intelligence at the summit dinner, but that is the president's own account rather than a record of the talks, so whether AI was addressed, and the Ukraine and economic points, stay open.
  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “they've got to use their leverage to end this war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.” Unsettled. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was sharply reduced but not stopped: UKMTO, as reported by Gulf News, put transits about 65% below pre-conflict levels and 'well below normal but not stalled', and Lloyd's List counted 550 non-Iranian-linked transits in October. That fits neither a closed strait nor normal operation, and the UKMTO figures could not be read directly from a UKMTO document.
  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “You saw before that the president and the current prime minister in Israel have indicated that they are planning to end the military aid that's existed for decades to Israel.” Unsettled. Trump said in a Fox News interview, as reported on Nov. 3, 2026, that he and Netanyahu agreed to stop the roughly $4 billion a year in aid, while Netanyahu's own stated position (January 2026) is to taper U.S. aid to zero within ten years. A plan to end aid fits Trump's remarks, but Netanyahu's position is a phase-down, and no direct Netanyahu confirmation of an end date was read; the current aid agreement runs through September 2028.

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 9 unsettled (Donald Trump, Ron Johnson, Steny Hoyer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: He reiterated Thursday that he and Xi agree Iran needs to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for world energy supplies that has become a chokepoint since the start of the war.” Unsupported. No Chinese record found states or rejects that Iran must fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz; the statement rests on Trump's own account. Searched: China's Foreign Ministry readouts of the Nov. 19 summit and bilateral meeting (which mention only that the Middle East was discussed), the joint declaration, and AP's report; Xinhua could not be loaded, and no Chinese-language record was searched.
  • Ron Johnson, U.S. Senator: “That is President Trump's power. He's exercising his constitutional authority” Unsettled. The War Powers Resolution, as held in AskAmerica's U.S. Code table, conditions the President's use of forces on a declaration of war, specific authorization or an attack on the United States (50 U.S.C. 1541(c)) and requires withdrawal within 60 days without authorization (1544(b)), but 1547(d) leaves each branch's constitutional authority unchanged. Congress has not authorized the war, the administration says hostilities have terminated and the resolution is unconstitutional, and no binding ruling on this war has settled the question.
  • Steny Hoyer, U.S. Representative: “Sadly, although President Trump signed that bill into law, just days later he turned around and did exactly the opposite of what the law called for when he waived--rather than imposed--the sanctions it anticipated.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's bill records show Trump signed H.R. 5334 on Sept. 18, 2026, and Executive Order 14436 of Oct. 16, 2026 waived its sanctions before they took effect. The signing and the waiver are confirmed; the waiver came 28 days after the signing, so whether that is "just days later" depends on how loosely the phrase is read.

Disagreements

  • Ron Johnson, U.S. Senator: “That is President Trump's power. He's exercising his constitutional authority” (unsettled)
    Tim Kaine, U.S. Senator: “the war was unconstitutional from the start because it was not a war of imminent defense and the President did not seek the congressional authorization required by the Constitution.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.” Unsettled. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in January 2026 that 20,000 to 25,000 Russian soldiers are killed each month, excluding the seriously wounded, while U.K. Ministry of Defence figures combine killed and wounded and other estimates found in search put deaths near 9,000 a month. The estimates straddle the line the test draws, so they do not decide it.

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump, Chuck Schumer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.” Unsettled. GCHQ's May 2026 annual lecture, read directly, says 'almost half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the conflict began', which averages about 10,000 deaths a month over the war but gives no current monthly rate. The U.K. Defence Ministry's monthly figures (about 31,000 in November 2025, as reported by Ukrinform) count killed and wounded together. No official deaths-only monthly estimate was found, so the claim is neither confirmed nor ruled out. The claim that the deaths created an opening to end the war was not assessed.
  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Trump arrived in Manila only 30 minutes before the summit ended and is off to China tomorrow to spend the rest of the week with Xi Jinping.” Unsettled. Pre-trip reports from AFP and from ANI (citing the White House) said Trump was due in Manila on the evening of Nov. 17, 'near the summit's conclusion', with a Nov. 18 Marcos visit and then Shenzhen, so the departure for China matches. No report found gives his actual landing time or when the summit closed, so '30 minutes' was neither confirmed nor ruled out.

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-16: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Pete Hegseth)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Pete Hegseth, U.S. Secretary of Defense: “Every once in a while you might have one, unfortunately we call it a squirter that makes its way through.” Unsettled. No official count of how many Iranian drones and missiles got past U.S. defenses in the war's first days was found. At the same briefing the chairman of the Joint Chiefs said U.S. systems had "intercepted hundreds of ballistic missiles"; launch totals attributed to the head of U.S. Central Command (more than 2,000 drones and 500 ballistic missiles, as reported by DefenseScoop) come with no matching intercept count. Defense Department pages refused the fetch, so the briefing was read from a copy of the transcript.
  • Pete Hegseth, U.S. Secretary of Defense: “And in that particular case it happened to hit a tactical operations center that was fortified.” Unsettled. No official description of the struck structure other than the secretary's own was found. CBS reports that the Army finished its investigation in June 2026 and that the Pentagon declined to say whether the unit was denied adequate force protection; no published report was found. In the CBS report a major from the unit says the protection there "was to stop car bombs and threats like that" with "nothing there designed to protect from an aerial attack", and describes the building as a "quadruple-wide trailer". Those are a witness's accounts, not an official record, and the answer may turn on what "fortified" covers.

item.title: Said & Checked, War and Foreign Affairs, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Marco Rubio, John Moolenaar, Mike Pence)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State: “The economic pain that we are inflicting on that regime is so great that there's no need for military action because we've weakened them so much,” Unsettled. IMF projections for 2026 show Iran's economy shrinking 7.6% with inflation averaging 78.6%, during a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports and added financial sanctions. No source read separates the damage done by economic measures from the damage done by seven months of war. The IMF figures were read through a summary of its data service, not the raw table.
  • John Moolenaar, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “So, anyone who doesn't comply with the CCP can be imprisoned, they or their family members.” Unsettled. The law, as quoted by Wikipedia, requires cooperation with intelligence work, but commentary cited there says it has no enforcement mechanism. No page read documents a person or a relative imprisoned for refusing to cooperate, and "anyone" is loose wording.
  • Mike Pence, Former Vice President of the United States: “for inexplicable reasons, we stopped after five weeks. We sunk their navy, we had complete air superiority, took down 15,000 military sites in Iran.” Unsettled. Defense News' report of the April 8, 2026 Pentagon briefing confirms a 38-day campaign, about five and a half weeks, ended by a ceasefire, with officials claiming 150 ships sunk. It gives no count of sites struck, and no official source for the 15,000 figure could be read.

Disagreements

  • Cory Booker, U.S. Senator from New Jersey: “And now he just wants to walk away.”
    Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State: “The economic pain that we are inflicting on that regime is so great that there's no need for military action because we've weakened them so much,” (premise unsettled)
    Both statements in context
